item.title: Thiophenol‐Catalyzed Anti‐Markovnikov Coupling of α‐Methylene‐γ‐Butenolides Under Visible Light: Total Synthesis of Aucklappalide A
item.description:
Visible-light thiophenol catalysis enables the first anti-Markovnikov intermolecular coupling of α-methylene-γ-butenolides under photocatalyst-free conditions. A sulfur-mediated photochemical manifold involving a competent thiophenol adduct promotes intermolecular C–C bond formation, providing concise access to complex disesquiterpenoid architectures, including aucklappalide A.


ABSTRACT

General methods for the selective anti-Markovnikov intermolecular coupling of electron-poor alkenes remain scarce. Herein, we report a visible-light-mediated, photocatalyst-free strategy for the anti-Markovnikov coupling of α-methylene-γ-butenolides using a simple formate/thiophenol reaction platform. The method enables the direct synthesis of structurally diverse homo- and cross-coupled disesquiterpenoid architectures from complex sesquiterpenoid lactones, including the first total synthesis of aucklappalide A. Mechanistic investigations support a distinct sulfur-mediated photochemical manifold involving a thiophenol adduct that provides access to the carbon-centered radical required for intermolecular C–C bond formation. These findings establish a photocatalyst-free approach to the redox-neutral anti-Markovnikov coupling of α-methylene-γ-butenolides, uncover a previously unrecognized sulfur-mediated radical manifold enabled by formate/thiophenol photochemistry, and suggest that related sulfur-centered radical processes may contribute to the biosynthesis of dimeric sesquiterpenoid lactones.

item.title: Catalytically Active Species and Sites in CO2 Hydrogenation Identified by Modulation Excitation Spectroscopy
item.description:
Rational design of better catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation requires detailed knowledge of the reaction mechanism including key intermediates and active sites. This Minireview discusses the potential of modulation excitation spectroscopy as a powerful tool to identify active species and sites as illustrated by the current literature, and gives an outlook on methodical extentions and applications beyond thermal catalysis.


ABSTRACT

Thermocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO2) hydrogenation has developed into an important sustainable route toward valuable fuels and chemicals, thereby reducing the greenhouse gas CO2 and supporting the energy transition. For a rational design of more efficient, selective, and stable catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation, detailed knowledge of the reaction mechanism, including key intermediates and active sites is required. Modulation excitation spectroscopy (MES) has emerged as a powerful tool to discriminate between catalytically active and (nonparticipating) spectator species and to identify active sites, and has been shown to provide important new mechanistic findings not accessible by steady-state approaches, contributing to the very intense debate on CO2 hydrogenation mechanisms. Despite its broad applicability, the MES method is still rarely used in catalysis research and has contributed to the mechanism of CO2 hydrogenation mainly by its combination with infrared spectroscopy. In this Minireview, the potential of MES for providing mechanistic insight on catalytic CO2 hydrogenation will be illustrated based on the current literature, followed by an outline of potential methodical extensions. Future prospects for the application of MES to mechanistic studies on CO2 activation beyond thermal catalysis, including photo- and electrocatalysis, as well as other areas of research will be discussed.

item.title: Guide DNAs Program Enzyme for Detection of Circulating Tumor DNA Without Target Denaturation and Amplification
item.description:
Chemically modified guide DNAs program λ exonuclease to access native double-stranded ctDNA at room temperature, enabling detection without target amplification or denaturation. Coupling this chemistry to a DNAzyme and single-molecule fluorescence readout supports sensitive EGFR L858R ctDNA analysis in plasma.


ABSTRACT

Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is fragmented, tumor-derived cell-free double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) whose low abundance and limited sequence accessibility complicate detection under mild conditions. Here we show that guide DNAs (gDNAs) can program an exonuclease to interrogate native dsDNA under mild conditions and convert this access into a single-molecule fluorescence readout. We found that gDNA 5′-terminal chemistry regulates λ exonuclease (λExo) recruitment. Among those termini, anionic 5′-phosphate and 5′-carboxyl-C10 phosphate enabled the strongest target-dependent processing. Molecular simulations suggested a possible structural basis for these activity differences based on terminal positioning within the catalytic pocket. Coupling the optimized 5′-carboxyl-C10 phosphate gDNA with 10–23 DNAzyme turnover generated a single-molecule fluorescence readout without target nucleic-acid amplification. The assay detected dsDNA down to 10 fM across 10–1000 fM, showed a statistically significant response at an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) L858R mutant fraction of 0.05% under the tested conditions, and was applied to 24 plasma samples (12 from patients with non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and 12 from healthy donors), achieving 91.7% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 95.8% accuracy, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.97. This work establishes gDNA-programmed enzyme access as a route for detecting low-abundance duplex tumor DNA.

item.title: Confinement Enables Direct Electrosynthesis of Acetaldoxime From CO and Nitrate
item.description:
We report a confinement-enhanced electrocatalytic route for acetaldoxime synthesis from CO and NO3 − via C–N coupling. By encapsulating ultrasmall Cu nanoparticles into SBA-15, the sluggish C–C dimerization is kinetically matched with rapid NO3 − reduction, favoring the oximation pathway and achieving a production rate of 255.1 mmol gcat. − 1 h− 1 with an 8.2% Faradaic efficiency, enabling sustainable co-upcycling of carbon and nitrogen wastes.


ABSTRACT

Aldoximes are vital feedstocks in the fields of medicine, agriculture, and industry, yet their conventional synthesis suffers from high environmental costs and carbon footprints. Here, we report a direct electrocatalytic route to acetaldoxime via CO and NO3 − co-reduction. The C–N coupling efficiency in this process hinges on the kinetic match between CO reduction and NO3 − reduction. Acetaldoxime synthesis exemplifies this challenge: sluggish C–C dimerization contrasts with rapid NO3 −RR, leading to over-reduction of nitrogen species to NH3. We hypothesized that a confinement strategy could selectively promote C–C dimerization and enrich acetaldehyde intermediate, thereby facilitating oximation. Ultrasmall Cu nanoparticles were encapsulated within SBA-15 mesopores to selectively accelerate the dimerization step. Combined operando Raman and in situ differential electrochemical mass spectrometry reveal that the confined Cu lowers the overpotential for the key C2 intermediate to align with that for NH2OH generation, enabling efficient C–N coupling to acetaldoxime. The optimized Cu@SBA-15 catalyst achieves an acetaldoxime production rate of 255.1 mmol gcat. − 1 h− 1 (partial current density: 24.6 mA cm− 2). This work establishes a sustainable pathway toward aldoximes, aligning with green chemistry principles while expanding the toolbox for electrocatalytic C–N bond formation.

item.title: An Acyclic Two‐Coordinate Stannyliumylidene Enables SnII/SnIV Redox Catalysis
item.description:
Less coordination, greater reactivity: An isolable, acyclic two-coordinate stannyliumylidene combines pronounced Lewis acidity with an accessible lone pair, enabling ambiphilic small-molecule activation. Its unusual electronic and structural flexibility unlocks Sn(II)/Sn(IV) redox catalysis in ketone hydrosilylation, supported by the isolation of a catalytically competent stannyliumylidene–ketone adduct and detailed mechanistic investigations.


ABSTRACT

Main-group redox catalysis hinges on a fundamental trade-off, that is, reactive p-block centres must be stable enough to isolate, yet flexible enough to cycle through oxidation states. In this regard, two-coordinate stannyliumylidene ions with an accessible lone pair and vacant p-orbital offer an attractive ambiphilic platform for engaging in redox processes. To date, most reported examples remain confined to π- or heteroatom-donor-stabilized rigid frameworks, and the isolation of a genuinely two-coordinate acyclic stannyliumylidene has remained elusive. Herein, we report the synthesis and isolation of a two-coordinate, acyclic, mono-N-heterocyclic-carbene-stabilized stannyliumylidene paired with a weakly coordinating [B(3,5-(CF3)2C6H3)4]− anion. Stripped of additional donor stabilization, the tin centre is rendered highly electrophilic while maintaining an accessible lone pair. This enhanced electrophilicity enabled capture of a stannyliumylidene–ketone adduct, the first structurally characterized ketone-bound tetryliumylidene intermediate that is directly implicated in a catalytic cycle. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, combining experimental results with theoretical calculations, reveal an Sn(II)/Sn(IV) redox manifold that drives catalytic turnover. Together, these results significantly expand the landscape of tin-based redox catalysis and highlight that accessing stable low-valent stannyliumylidene ions with a minimal coordination number and weaker donor stabilization is a feasible approach for unlocking transition-metal-like redox behaviour at the tin centre.

item.title: Radical Buffering by Isolated Ru and Fe Sites in ZSM‐5 for Selective Methane Oxidation to Formic Acid
item.description:
In ZSM-5 micropores, two independent single-atom populations cooperate without any metal–metal bond. Fe activates methane to methyl radicals while Ru activates H2O2 and buffers hydroxyl radicals. This radical buffering directs Eley-Rideal coupling toward formic acid, raising oxygenate productivity 2.2-fold over Fe/ZSM-5 under mild conditions.


ABSTRACT

The selective conversion of methane under mild conditions is limited by the uncontrolled reactivity of radical intermediates (·CH3, ·OH) generated during Fe-catalyzed oxidation with H2O2. Here we report a radical buffering strategy in which atomically dispersed Ru is co-loaded with Fe in ZSM-5 as an ·OH reservoir, steering intermediates toward selective Eley-Rideal-type coupling in the micropores. The Ru-Fe/ZSM-5 catalyst achieves an oxygenate productivity of 37.5 mmol·gcat −1·h−1 at 70°C with 95.7% oxygenate selectivity and 92.3% formic acid selectivity among liquid products, a 2.2-fold improvement over Fe/ZSM-5. Extended X-ray absorption fine structure analysis shows that Ru and Fe exist as two independent populations of single atoms with no metal–metal bonding. Electron paramagnetic resonance and in situ infrared spectroscopy show that Fe activates CH4 to ·CH3 while Ru activates H2O2 and holds part of the resulting ·OH. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that Ru binds ·OH more strongly than Fe (−3.130 compared to −2.738 eV), and dissociates H2O2 nearly thermoneutrally (+0.077 eV). Therefore ·OH is held on Ru rather than on the Fe. This work establishes radical buffering by independent single-atom populations in confined micropores as a design principle for controlling selectivity in radical-mediated catalysis.

item.title: Alternating Terpolymerization of CO2 With Cyclosilanes and Epoxides to A‐B‐C‐Sequenced Recyclable Poly(silyl ether–ester)
item.description:
Catalyzed alternating terpolymerization of CO2, cyclosilanes, and epoxides, driven by thermodynamically favorable silyl ether bond formation, produces A-B-C sequence-defined poly(silyl ether–ester)s with tunable structures and thermal properties as well as chemical recyclability and hydrolytic degradability under acidic or basic conditions.


ABSTRACT

Carbon dioxide (CO2)-derived polyesters represent an attractive yet underdeveloped class of sustainable polymers, with most existing CO2-based polyesters relying on carbonate linkages in their backbones with statistical or block sequences. Here, we introduce terpolymerization of CO2 with cyclosilanes and epoxides to access poly(silyl ether–ester) with perfectly alternating A-B-C (CO2-alt-cyclosilane-alt-epoxide) sequences. This terpolymerization is enabled by the thermodynamically favored formation of Si─O bonds, providing a driving force for efficient incorporation of both silalactones and epoxides into the terpolymer backbone in an alternating fashion. A range of epoxide and silacyclobutane substrates can be incorporated into the polyester, affording structurally diverse terpolymers. Notably, these polymers are stable thermally (T d up to 313°C) and hydrolytically (in neutral water) but can slowly degrade under acidic or basic conditions and be chemically depolymerized under mild catalytic conditions to recover the silalactone monomer.

item.title: Standardization Transformation of Softwood Protolignin to Benzoxazole Molecule With Tumor‐Selective Cytotoxicity
item.description:
The standardization transformation of softwood protolignin into the bioactive benzoxazole molecule C3-GLB-pCBA with tumor-selective cytotoxicity was first established.


ABSTRACT

The protolignin standardization transformation into high-value-added pharmaceutical chemicals requires elaborate strategy design and catalytic system construction. Herein, a novel lignin valorization pattern to produce G-lignin-derived benzoxazoles from softwood is achieved, which involves the tandem CRF transformation of lignocellulose to C3-alkyl guaiacol (C3-G), stoichiometric diazotization-reductive ammonification of C3-G to aminophenol C3-GAP, and photocatalytic cyclization of C3-GAP to the benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA. The whole process can yield 6.2 wt% benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA from the aromatic guaiacyl rings of the original softwood lignin. Furthermore, the in vitro cytotoxicity assays with human osteosarcoma (HOS) cells, normal human osteoblast cells (hFOB1.19), and mouse 3T3 fibroblasts confirm the potential tumor-selective cytotoxicity of the as-synthesized G-lignin-derived benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA. Further TEA and LCA indicate the sustainability of the synthesis process of C3-GLB-pCBA from softwood. The success of the tandem pattern may inspire further studies on the high-value utilization of lignin to produce pharmaceutical molecules.

item.title: Dual‐Force Strategy for Universal Clusteroluminescence in Non‐Conjugated Small Molecules
item.description:
A DETA-induced universal luminescence (DIUL) strategy converts non-conjugated, non-emissive small molecules into bright clusteroluminescent materials. Synergistic ionic (─BF4 −/─NH2 +) and hydrogen-bonding (─NH─/─NH2) dual forces drive through-space conjugation, yielding >70% quantum yields in water. The resulting probes enable high-contrast dual-color cellular, 3D tumor spheroid, and long-term zebrafish imaging, establishing a modular platform for non-traditional luminophores in bioimaging.


ABSTRACT

Non-traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π-conjugation are attractive for bio-applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non-luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a modular strategy based on the diethylenetriamine (DETA)-induced universal luminescence (DIUL) effect, which converts simple non-conjugated precursors into highly emissive cluster-based small molecules via synergistic dual-force: ionic (─BF4 −/─NH2 +) and hydrogen-bonding (─NH─/─NH2) interactions. The resulting seven derivatives exhibit >70% photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) in water, with emission independent of ring/chain structure, demonstrating a robust dual-force mechanism that advances beyond hydrogen-bond-dominated aggregation-induced emission (AIE) models. These probes show excellent water solubility, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling high-contrast dual-color cellular and deep 3D tumor spheroid imaging, along with long-term biocompatible zebrafish imaging. This work establishes a versatile modular functionalization platform for bright NTLs, offering fundamental insights into cooperative non-covalent interactions and opening new avenues for designing multifunctional optical materials in bioimaging, sensing, and encryption.

item.title: Advancing C3 Polymerization of Alkynylcyclopropanes via a Synergistic Lewis Acid/Brønsted Base/C(sp3)–H Bond System
item.description:
The high electronegativity and strong coordinating ability of C–C triple bonds often hinder their integration into donor-acceptor cyclopropane chemistry. Here, we establish a synergistic Lewis acid/Brønsted base/C(sp3)─H bond system that overcomes these intrinsic limitations, enabling controlled C3 polymerization of alkynylcyclopropanes (ACPs) and providing access to a series of advanced functional polymeric materials.


ABSTRACT

The integration of cyclopropane chemistry with polymer science could offer access to unique all-carbon polymers. However, the ring-opening polymerization (ROP) of cyclopropanes generally requires strong electron-donating and -withdrawing substituents, limiting the use of electronically less activated monomers such as 2-alkynylcyclopropane-1,1-dicarboxylates (ACPs). Here, we demonstrate that the synergistic combination of a Lewis acid and a Brønsted base overcomes the electronic limitations imposed by carbon–carbon triple bonds, including their high electronegativity and strong coordinating ability, enabling the unprecedented C3 ROP of ACPs. This process is regulated by a reversible-deactivation equilibrium mediated by chain-end C(sp3)─H bonds, affording well-defined polymers bearing alkyne side groups. The resulting functional polymers provide a versatile platform for applications ranging from stimulus-responsive sensing to Raman imaging.

item.title: [8+4]‐Connected Ether‐Oxygen‐Based 3D COF Redox Mediators for Durable Light‐Assisted Indirect Electrocatalysis
item.description:
A series of [8+4]-connected 3D COFs, TADM–TAPP–COF (M) (M = Ni, Mn, and Cu), has been constructed from ether-oxygen-based 8-connected ether-oxygen based building blocks and metalloporphyrin linkers that can serve as redox mediators for the highly durable light-assisted indirect electrocatalytic condensation cyclization reaction.


ABSTRACT

Ether-oxygen is a type of functional group with high chemical stability, electronic modulation capability, and imparted molecular flexibility, yet incorporating ether-oxygen groups into high-connectivity covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to explore their extended applications remains a challenge. Herein, we have designed a series of [8+4]-connected 3D COFs with scu topology, named TADM–TAPP–COF(M) (M = Ni, Mn, and Cu), by introducing eight-connected ether-oxygen based building blocks and metalloporphyrin nodes, which can be applied in high-stability light-assisted indirect electrocatalysis. These 3D COFs exhibit good crystallinity, nanosheet morphology, flexible 3D pore structure, abundant ether-oxygen groups and active metal sites, and excellent electrolyte affinity, which can act as efficient redox mediators. Impressively, the Ni-incorporated structure TADM–TAPP–COF (Ni) demonstrates high yield in the condensation cyclization reaction of aromatic aldehydes and 2-aminobenzenethiol to produce 2-phenylbenzothiazole (yields up to 96%), coupled with the simultaneous production of gas-phase H2 product (∼1.15 mmol g−1 h−1). Notably, it also shows remarkable stability (continuous reaction for 300 h), high recyclability (8 cycles), and scale-up production ability (about 2 g in a 12 h batch experiment) and wide substrate applicability, providing a valuable example for the structural design of catalysts toward light-assisted indirect electrocatalysis.

item.title: Heat‐Activated Reversible Conjugation Switching in Polymers Through Cooperative Ion Pairing
item.description:
A general cooperative ion-pair-regulated strategy for reversibly generating linear conjugation in polymers was developed to achieve reversible colorless-to-colored heat-activated behavior. Weakly coordinated alkali metal salts such as LiPF6 and NaPF6 promote lactone ring opening to generate thermally activated multicolor responses and rewritable invisible inks, while isopropanol coordination reversibly restores the nonconjugated colorless state.


ABSTRACT

Thermochromic conjugated polymers generally undergo transitions from colored to less-colored states upon heating due to disruption of π-conjugation. In contrast, heat-triggered switching from a colorless state to a more intensely colored conjugated state remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a reversible conjugation-switching polymer system governed by cooperative interactions between metal cations and counteranions. By incorporating lactone-functionalized xanthene units directly into conjugated polymer backbones, weakly solvated Li+, Na+, and Ag+ ions, acting cooperatively with their weakly coordinating counteranions, induce lactone ring opening and establish linear conjugation along the polymer backbone, thereby producing pronounced optical responses. Coordination of the metal ions by isopropanol reverses the process and restores the colorless state. A series of conjugated copolymers displayed thermally activated multicolor responses spanning blue, green, yellow, orange, red, magenta, and black, enabling rewritable invisible-ink systems on paper substrates. Density functional theory calculations support a nearly barrierless Li+/PF6 − ion-pair-cooperation-promoted ring-opening process and reveal reversible switching between twisted nonconjugated and planar linearly conjugated states. These results establish a metal-ion-regulated conjugation-switching strategy for heat-activated colorless-to-colored switching and responsive optical materials.

item.title: Photoreduction of Chlorinated Volatile Waste Into C2+ Hydrocarbons
item.description:
We report here synthesis of the first nickel–sulfur anthraquinone complex and the first photoreduction system to convert a series of chlorinated volatile organic compounds into unsaturated C2+ hydrocarbons using visible light. The photocatalytic system is not only tolerant to the difficultly converted substrates with high chlorine content but also capable of generating multi-carbon products from the C1 compounds.


ABSTRACT

Chlorinated volatile organic compounds (Cl─VOCs) are a class of major environmental pollutants and potential human carcinogens. Dechlorination of Cl─VOC waste into harmless and value-added chemicals under mild conditions is highly desirable yet challenging, and cannot be achieved using current photocatalytic methods. Here, we report the synthesis of the first nickel anthraquinone–thiolate complex for photoreduction of a variety of Cl─VOCs into unsaturated C2+ hydrocarbons in good yields using visible light. Notably, the molecular system is capable of both reducing C2 Cl─VOCs with high chlorine content into acetylene and C─C coupling of C1 Cl─VOCs into ethylene and propylene. Mechanistic studies reveal that multielectron and multi-proton reduction of the nickel complex is critical in generating the catalytically active species for various reductive dechlorination transformations. This study provides a blueprint for the conversion of chlorinated waste into highly valuable chemicals using solar energy.

item.title: Single‐Atom Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption Enables Ultrafast Charge Transfer for Boosting Photocatalytic H2 Production
item.description:
Single-atom Ni (NiSA) cocatalysts spontaneously form a multi-hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalysis, creating a local electron-deficient environment. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration induces stronger d-p orbital hybridization across the NiSA–S interface, shortens the Ni–S bond, and builds a highly conductive charge-transfer channel for ultrafast electron extraction from CdS, thus driving efficient photocatalytic H2 evolution.


ABSTRACT

Single-atom cocatalysts with near-100% atom utilization are widely studied for boosting photocatalytic H2 evolution, but their mechanistic insights remain largely restricted to idealized mono-hydrogen adsorption models. Such simplified frameworks fail to capture the complexity of operando reaction environments, where the high coordination unsaturation of single atoms inevitably drives a transition toward multi-hydrogen adsorption states. Here, we demonstrate that an N-coordinated Ni single-atom cocatalyst (NiSA-N) forms a multi-hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalytic H2 evolution, significantly accelerating ultrafast charge transfer kinetics. Research results demonstrate that the adsorption of multiple hydrogen triggers spontaneous free-electron delocalization, rendering the Ni center into a unique electron-deficient (δ+) feature. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration enhances the interfacial d-p orbital hybridization between NiSA and S of CdS, effectively shortening the interfacial Ni–S bond to construct a highly conductive channel that facilitates ultrafast electron transfer from the CdS to NiSA cocatalyst, as elucidated by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Consequently, the NiSA-N/CdS system achieves an exceptional H2 evolution rate of 20.20 mmol h−1 g−1. This work identifies the multi-hydrogen adsorption state as a pivotal nexus linking surface chemistry to ultrafast dynamics, providing a conceptual framework for engineering high-performance catalysts for artificial photosynthesis.

item.title: Localized Dipoles Enable Synergistic Kinetic and Thermodynamic Piezoreforming of Waste Plastics
item.description:
This work presents a mechanically driven piezocatalytic reforming method for converting waste plastics into platform chemicals carbon monoxide (CO) under ambient conditions. Asymmetric Fe–Se–Mo channel induces local dipoles, kinetically suppressing carrier recombination and accelerating charge-proton transfer, while thermodynamically enhancing the adsorption of key intermediates and lowering the activation energy barrier. Therefore, we achieved a 30.5 times higher CO yield with stable long-term production compared to MoSe2 catalysts.


ABSTRACT

The piezocatalytic plastic wastes into clean fuels at ambient conditions offers considerable promise, but hindering by both rapid carrier recombination in kinetics and slow surface reactions in thermodynamics. Here, we present a conceptually distinct strategy to simultaneously tackle both core challenges by tailoring localized dipole via anchoring FeSe2 nanoclusters onto MoSe2 piezocatalysts. These clusters induce localized lattice distortions via strong metal-support interaction, generating localized dipole that serve a dual function. Kinetically, localized dipole can effectively capture the electrons excited by piezoelectricity, suppressing recombination and establishing a dominant, long-lived interfacial charge transfer channel directly to the reactants. Thermodynamically, localized dipole can lower the d-band center of the active sites, enhance the adsorption of reaction intermediates, and significantly reduce the activation energy barrier of key intermediates. Therefore, the optimized catalyst exhibits carbon monoxide (CO) evolution of 87.65 µmol·g−1 with high selectivity in the piezocatalytic peroxydisulfate (PDS) system, 30.5 times that of MoSe2. Importantly, after simple pretreatment of polylactic acid (PLA), the CO production reaches 1886.55 µmol·g−1 with stable long-term performance. This work elucidates the fundamental role of localized dipole in harmonizing charge dynamics with surface catalysis, providing an effective approach for designing highly efficient and durable piezocatalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

item.title: Entropy‐Compensated Electrolyte Enables Low‐Temperature 400 Wh Kg−1 Silicon‐Based Lithium‐Ion Batteries
item.description:
An entropy-compensation strategy is introduced to regulate low-temperature solvation in Si-anode electrolytes. Enhanced solvation entropy preserves small anion-rich clusters, accelerates bulk Li+ transport, and stabilizes interfacial reactions. This strategy enables pouch cells to achieve both excellent low-temperature cycling performance and a high energy density of up to 400 Wh kg−1.


ABSTRACT

Electrolytes dictate the low-temperature (LT) performance of Si-anode lithium-ion batteries, wherein bulk solvation governs Li+ transport and interfacial stability. Especially, enlarged ionic clusters and strengthened ion pairing at LT hinder Li+ migration, limiting Li+ supply to the interface and destabilizing interfacial reactions. Herein, we propose an entropy-compensation strategy to counteract LT-induced solvation deterioration in Si-anode electrolytes. Increasing the solvation entropy (ΔS solv) compensates for the LT-induced increase in the Gibbs free-energy change for ion-cluster dissociation (ΔG solv), thereby raising the corresponding equilibrium constant (K solv) and suppressing ion pairing. Consequently, electrolytes preferentially form smaller anion-rich ionic clusters, delivering an approximately threefold increase in ionic conductivity at −20°C. Enhanced bulk transport alleviates concentration polarization, stabilizes the interfacial solvation environment, and promotes uniform SEI-forming reactions. Benefiting from this coupled bulk-interfacial optimization, Ah-level pouch cells retain 97.8% capacity after 165 cycles at −20°C and support sustained discharge at −81°C. This strategy enables high-energy pouch cells to deliver 400 Wh kg−1 under ambient conditions and 339 Wh kg−1 at LT, while an Ah-level pouch cell retains 80% capacity after 1150 cycles at 2 C. This work identifies ΔS solv as a critical thermodynamic descriptor for low-temperature electrolyte design.

item.title: Cryptochiral Circularly Polarized Luminescence Emerges From Cosolvent‐Regulated Pathway Complexity in Amyloidogenic Peptide Self‐Assembly
item.description:
Can a material emit circularly polarized light without ground-state chirality? Cosolvent-regulated pathway complexity in a naphthalimide–peptide conjugate reveals a cryptochiral circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) state: Strong CPL despite undetectable ground-state chirality. Thermal annealing or aging transforms kinetically trapped spherical nanoassemblies into chiral nanofibers, offering a pathway to adaptive chiroptical materials.


ABSTRACT

Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) is important for chiral photonics, optical encryption, bioimaging, and information processing. It is usually associated with an identifiable chiral ground-state organization, and CPL without detectable ground-state chirality remains comparatively unexplored. Herein, we report a rare “cryptochiral CPL” phenomenon arising from cosolvent-regulated pathway complexity in the self-assembly of a naphthalimide (NMI)-amyloidogenic peptide conjugate (PEP-L). In water, PEP-L spontaneously forms thermodynamically stable, emissive nanofibers with pronounced supramolecular chirality and strong CPL. Adding a small amount of cosolvent redirects assembly toward kinetically trapped spherical nanoassemblies and shows no detectable Circular Dichroism (CD) response in the naphthalimide chromophore region, but retains pronounced CPL, which decouples ground-state and excited-state chiroptical responses. We term this behavior cryptochiral CPL. Thermal annealing or aging converts the spheres into thermodynamically favored nanofibers with distinct CD and CPL characteristics. The enantiomer PEP-D shows mirror-image chiroptical responses, which validates the phenomenon. Density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations under different conditions give molecular-level insight into the conformation, noncovalent interactions, and supramolecular organization of the different assembly states. These findings establish a new conceptual framework for adaptive chiral photonic materials and open opportunities for hidden optical encoding and biomolecular photonic systems.

item.title: Dual‐DUBTACs Enable Targeted Protein Stabilization via Multi‐DUB Engagement
item.description:
Dual-DUBTACs enable targeted protein stabilization by recruiting multiple deubiquitinases. By engaging USP5 and USP9X, these compounds promote the deubiquitination and stabilization of CFTR and cGAS. Compared with conventional single-DUBTACs, this strategy offers greater flexibility in DUB recruitment and provides a promising avenue for restoring the stability of disease-relevant proteins.


ABSTRACT

Targeted protein stabilization has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for restoring the abundance and function of disease-relevant proteins. Deubiquitinase-targeting chimeras (DUBTACs) offer a chemical approach to protein stabilization by recruiting deubiquitinases (DUBs) to promote target deubiquitination. However, current DUBTAC strategies generally rely on the recruitment of a single DUB, leaving the potential of engaging multiple DUBs through a common recruiter largely unexplored. Here, we report a dual-DUBTAC strategy that enables targeted protein stabilization through the recruitment of two distinct DUBs. Using Degrasyn, a small-molecule reversible covalent inhibitor of multiple DUBs, as a privileged scaffold, we engineered small molecules that selectively stabilize CFTR and cGAS and demonstrate that these compounds enhance target protein homeostasis through USP9X- and USP5-mediated deubiquitination in cells. By decoupling substrate stabilization from reliance on a single DUB, the Dual-DUB platform confers adaptability across diverse ubiquitin chain architectures and rewired proteostasis networks characteristic of heterogeneous tumors and could overcome potential drug resistance in future clinical applications. This strategy expands the chemical space for restoring protective proteins and establishes a general framework for functional reactivation of destabilized tumor-suppressive pathways.

item.title: Solvent‐Removal‐Induced Lattice Reconstruction Enables Tunable Mn2+ Luminescence in Hybrid [MnBr4]2− for 3D X‐Ray Imaging
item.description:
This article reports that lattice ethanol acts as a reversible supramolecular switch in Mn(II)-based hybrid metal halides. Ethanol removal induces a single-crystal-to-single-crystal transformation, strengthens the Mn2 + crystal field, shifts emission from green to yellow-green, and enables efficient scintillation for X-ray detection and 3D imaging.


ABSTRACT

It is challenging to understand how noncoordinating lattice guests regulate Mn2+ luminescence without changing the metal coordination environment. Herein, we report a solvent-removal-induced single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SCSC) transformation from ethanol-containing (C33H29NP)2MnBr4·EtOH (CZTPPM) to the solvent-free phase (C33H29NP)2MnBr4 (CZTPPM1). Ethanol removal preserves the configuration of isolated [MnBr4]2− tetrahedra while inducing lattice contraction, hydrogen-bonding network reorganization, and enhanced tetrahedral distortion. As a result, the emission undergoes a distinct green (518 nm) to yellow-green (543 nm) shift. Combined low-temperature excitation spectroscopy, crystal-field analysis, electron-phonon coupling evaluation, and excited-state decay kinetics establish a correlation between supramolecular lattice reconstruction, local ligand-field modulation, and excited-state relaxation. Furthermore, the solvent-free phase retains efficient scintillation performance (including light yield of 56, 516 photons MeV−1 and detection limit of 59.97 nGyair s−1) and enables high-resolution static X-ray imaging and 3D X-ray reconstruction. This work provides insight into noncoordinating-guest-mediated crystal-field regulation and demonstrates its potential for developing multifunctional luminescent materials for radiation imaging.

item.title: Interfacial Molecular Engineering Mediated Intramolecular Inter‐Group Relay Effect Enables Efficient Acidic CO2‐to‐C2+ Conversion
item.description:
To enable high-selectivity C2+ production in acidic CO2RR, an SBMA molecule modification strategy establishes an intramolecular inter-group relay catalytic system on Cu. The adjacent ─N+(CH3)2─ and SO3- groups regulate *CO accumulation and interfacial proton transfer, promoting *OC─CHO coupling and C2+ formation. The Cu─SBMA catalyst delivers a C2+ FE of 90.4% at 0.8 A cm−2 and a SPCE of 92.8% at 0.6 A cm−2, while maintaining 85.3% C2+ FE at 0.4 A cm−2 under diluted CO2 conditions.


ABSTRACT

Electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) in acidic media represents an attractive strategy for improving carbon utilization efficiency by suppressing carbonate formation. However, achieving highly selective C2+ products at high current densities remains a formidable challenge due to the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and sluggish C─C coupling process. Here, we introduce the surface-adsorbed bifunctional organic molecule on Cu (Cu─SBMA), which delivers a Faradaic efficiency of 90.4% for C2+ products at 0.8 A cm−2 under acid media and pure CO2 flow, together with a single-pass carbon efficiency (SPCE) of 92.8% at 0.6 A cm−2. Furthermore, under diluted CO2 flow (15 vol% CO2), Cu─SBMA still maintains a high C2+ Faradaic efficiency of 85.3% at 0.4 A cm−2. Operando spectroscopy and DFT calculations uncover an intramolecular inter-group relay mechanism that governs asymmetrical OC─CHO coupling toward C2+ productions. Specifically, the quaternary ammonium (─N+(CH3)2─) group promotes CO2 activation and stabilizes *CO intermediate, the adjacent sulfonate (SO3 −) moiety mediates protonation of *CO toward *CHO. The intramolecular inter-group relay effect facilitates C─C coupling and suppresses HER. Our findings provide novel insights for the precise design of catalysts to regulate the reaction selectivity of complex multi-step energy conversion process.

item.title: Biomimetic N‐Terminal Homologation of Amino Acids
item.description:
The homologation of amino acids is a pivotal strategy used in lead optimization and molecular discovery, yet the preparation of β2-amino acids – via homologation of the N-terminus – remains underexplored. This methodology leverages a biomimetic radical translocation cascade driven by single-electron transfer. This enables direct access to diverse cyclic and acyclic β2-amino acids and phosphonates, unlocking new synthetic opportunities within drug discovery programs.


ABSTRACT

Homologation is a key tactic used in the lead optimization of small-molecule pharmaceuticals due to the potent impact such modifications can have on target affinity and physicochemical properties. However, while many elegant homologation strategies have been developed for the synthesis of β3-amino acids via decarboxylation, preparation of the β2-amino acid homologues remains underexplored. We report a general biomimetic strategy for the N-terminal homologation of amino acids using photoredox catalysis. Key to the success of this approach is a radical translocation cascade driven by single-electron transfer. This methodology provides streamlined access to a range of cyclic and acyclic β2-amino acids and phosphonates, providing new synthetic opportunities within drug discovery programs.

item.title: Precisely Recyclable, Multifunctional, and High‐Performance Polyester Integrated by a Single Imidazolium‐Monomer
item.description:
This work achieves the integration of green preparation, multifunctionality, high performance and precise recyclability for polyesters by introducing a single imidazolium-monomer. The imidazolium unit not only controls the C(alkyl)─O cleavage for flame retardancy but also catalyzes the C(carbonyl)─O cleavage for chemical recycling, paving the way for sustainable lifecycle management of polymer materials.


ABSTRACT

Sustainable lifecycle management of polymer materials urgently requires integrating green synthesis, service-stage desired properties, and end-of-life easy recyclability. Herein, by introducing a single imidazolium-monomer, the all-in-one integration of green preparation (without solvents or additives), multifunctionality (flame retardancy and antistatic property), high performance (excellent chromaticity, high heat resistance and high strength), and precise recyclability (in mixed wastes) for polyesters is achieved, which also reduces the health risks caused by additive migration. The key is that the imidazolium unit can not only control the C(alkyl)─O cleavage at high temperature to hinder polyester combustion but also catalyze the C(carbonyl)─O cleavage at the ester site to achieve chemical recycling of polyester. Without halogen or phosphorus elements, the polyester exhibits excellent chromaticity (L* value > 89 and b* value < 7), high glass-transition temperature (75°C), increased strength (78.8 MPa), antistatic function (surface resistivity as low as 6 × 1011 Ω), flame retardancy (the best UL-94 V-0 rating) and precise recycling in extremely complex mixed polymer wastes. This work successfully achieves lifecycle management of polyester materials via a single imidazolium-monomer, providing a feasible platform for the next generation of sustainable, multifunctional and high-performance polymer materials.

item.title: Atomic‐Scale Origin of Charge Density Wave–Driven Metal–Semiconductor Transition in an Incommensurately Modulated Metal–Organic Framework
item.description:
Single-crystal x-ray diffraction resolves the incommensurate modulation of Pr3HHTP2, linking its temperature-dependent structural evolution to a metal–semiconductor transition near 350 K. Hydration influences both the extent of modulation recovery and electrical conductivity. Combined structural and transport measurements support the proposed one-dimensional charge-density-wave mechanism, providing atomic-scale insight into electron–lattice coupling in conductive metal–organic frameworks.


ABSTRACT

Although metal–organic frameworks are widely recognized for their long-range crystalline periodicity, they can also exhibit intrinsic aperiodic structures associated with incommensurate modulation, whose observation has been exceptionally rare. In low-dimensional condensed matter physics, these unique structures often give rise to novel physical phenomena such as charge density wave. However, owing to limited direct experimental evidence, the relationship between incommensurate structural modulation and temperature-dependent electronic transport in conductive metal–organic frameworks remains incompletely understood. Here, using high-quality Pr3HHTP2 (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene) single crystals as a model system, we resolve the incommensurately modulated structure at 100 K (modulation vector q = 0.39143(12) c *) via temperature-dependent single-crystal x-ray diffraction. The observed reversible metal–semiconductor transition near 350 K occurs in a similar temperature range to the disappearance of the structural modulation, supporting a connection between lattice distortion and electronic behavior. The modulation reappears upon cooling, with guest water molecules influencing both the extent of its recovery and the electrical conductivity of the material. This work establishes a concrete experimental criterion for one-dimensional charge density wave in metal-organic frameworks and provides an ideal platform for probing coupled electronic–lattice modulations.

item.title: Coupling Iodine Regulation With Hole‐Selective Interfaces for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
item.description:
Phenothiazine/phenoxazine-tailored amidinium iodide salts, PTZ-PEFAI and PXZ-PEFAI, are designed and adopted as multifunctional interfacial modifiers that combine iodine regulation with favorable interfacial energetics and defect passivation in n–i–p perovskite solar cells. PTZ-PEFAI-incorporated devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.34% and excellent photothermal stability with a T 85 lifetime under maximum-power-point tracking at 65°C after 1500 h.


ABSTRACT

Operational instability remains a major barrier to the practical application of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), where the formation and volatilization of molecular iodine (I2) cause irreversible degradation of both the perovskite and adjacent hole-transport layer (HTL). Existing iodine-trapping or reducing agents can mitigate this degradation, but often compromise interfacial charge transport. Here, we develop two amidinium-based interfacial modifiers, PTZ-PEFAI and PXZ-PEFAI, that combine iodine regulation, favorable energy-level alignment, and defect passivation. Density functional theory calculations and experiments show that the S/O sites of phenothiazine (PTZ) and phenoxazine (PXZ) interact with I2 through halogen bonding, enabling I2 capture and dissociation. The direct identification of I3 − in modifier-iodine cocrystals further supports the regeneration of iodide ions. At the perovskite surface, these interactions suppress iodine loss, replenish iodide, and promote healing of iodine-vacancy defects. Meanwhile, the p-type PTZ/PXZ functionalities improve energy-level alignment and facilitate hole extraction at the perovskite/HTL interface. Consequently, PTZ-PEFAI-treated n–i–p PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.34% and a T 85 lifetime exceeding 1500 h under maximum-power-point tracking at 65°C. This work provides a molecular design strategy for simultaneously regulating interfacial iodine chemistry and charge transport toward efficient and stable PSCs.

item.title: Indirect Characterization of 14N Nuclei via 1H‐Detected Rotating‐Frame Relaxometry
item.description:
Fast-relaxing 14N nuclei can be indirectly characterized with enhanced sensitivity by introducing the scalar relaxation into the rotating-frame relaxation of J-coupled 1H nuclei from which nitrogen chemical shifts, one- or two-bond scalar couplings and polarization lifetimes can be derived.


ABSTRACT

14N NMR is notoriously difficult to perform in liquids due to the very fast spin relaxation and the large quadrupolar couplings, which render many signals invisible. We show here how 14N nuclei of biomolecular constituents can be probed indirectly by reintroducing the scalar relaxation of the second kind contribution as a relaxation pathway for J-coupled protons in double resonance spin-locking experiments. The enhanced 1H relaxation rates in the rotating-frame allow for direct evaluation of nitrogen chemical shifts and polarization lifetimes, from which one- and even two-bond 1H-14N scalar couplings as well as 14N quadrupolar interactions can be determined. We demonstrate the versatility of this method by characterizing 1H-14N spin pairs in several molecules of biological importance, showing proton relaxation enhancements beyond one order of magnitude. We further observe a pronounced effect from intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Our approach can be readily integrated into existing liquid-state NMR methodologies, as demonstrated here for 1H-detected relaxation-editing experiments with water suppression. This method provides access to nitrogen's picosecond-modulated quadrupolar interaction via sensitive proton detection in systems that would otherwise yield almost no detectable direct 14N signal even after averaging over thousands of transients.

item.title: Molten‐Salt Surface Restructuring of 3D‐Printed Agitator Exposes Ni0 Active Sites for Efficient Selective Alkyne Hydrogenation
item.description:
A 3D-printed blade-like agitator catalyst is created via molten-salt activation. It serves as both stirrer and catalyst, with enriched Ni0 sites and enhanced mass transfer. The device achieves 97% yield for selective hydrogenation of 2-butyne-1,4-diol to 1,4-butanediol.


ABSTRACT

Three-dimensional (3D) printing enables the integration of structural engineering with catalytic functionality, yet extending this concept to high-pressure liquid-phase hydrogenation remains challenging because catalytic efficiency, selectivity, and structural robustness are difficult to optimize simultaneously. Here, we report a strategy that couples additive manufacturing with molten-salt activation to engineer a 3D-printed bladed agitator catalyst (AB–MSL–H2). Molten-salt treatment selectively reconstructs the alloy surface while preserving the printed architecture, generating a Ni-enriched interface with abundant exposed metallic Ni0 active sites. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that surface reconstruction enriches accessible Ni0 sites to direct the desired hydrogenation pathway while suppressing isomerization, cyclization, and hydrogenolysis, whereas the integrated bladed architecture simultaneously enhances gas-liquid-solid mass transfer and reactant accessibility. Consequently, AB–MSL–H2 achieves complete conversion of 2-butyne-1,4-diol with a 1,4-butanediol yield exceeding 97%. This work establishes a general strategy for transforming additively manufactured structural alloys into catalytically active reactor components through molten-salt-induced surface reconstruction, expanding the scope of catalyst-reactor integration for high-pressure liquid-phase catalysis.

item.title: Synergistic Lewis Base Organocatalysis and Electrocatalysis for the Enantioselective Construction of α‐Fluorinated Quaternary Stereocenters
item.description:
Combining chiral isothiourea (ITU) organocatalysis with electrochemistry enables the enantioselective radical cross-coupling of fluorinated acetic esters with silyl enol ethers and allylsilanes. This synergistic strategy generates α-carbonyl tertiary radicals via anodic oxidation of C1-ammonium enolates and constructs sterically congested α-fluorinated quaternary stereocenters in high yields (up to 95%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee), offering a sustainable platform for valuable chiral fluorinated molecules.


ABSTRACT

The construction of α-fluorinated quaternary stereocenters—a structural motif of high value in pharmaceuticals and bioactive molecules—remains a formidable synthetic challenge due to inherent steric and stereoelectronic constraints. Herein, we report a synergistic strategy combining chiral isothiourea (ITU) organocatalysis with electrochemistry, enabling the direct and highly enantioselective α-alkylation of bench-stable fluorinated acetic esters with both silyl enol ethers and allylsilanes. This approach integrates anodic single-electron oxidation with asymmetric Lewis base catalysis, converting in situ-generated disubstituted C1-ammonium enolates into configurationally well-defined, chiral ITU-bound α-carbonyl tertiary radical intermediates. Subsequent stereocontrolled radical cross-coupling with SOMOphilic partners furnishes a broad range of esters bearing α-fluorinated quaternary stereocenters in high yields (up to 95%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). This work not only fills a significant gap in the single-electron chemistry of disubstituted C1-ammonium enolates but also provides a versatile platform for the rapid assembly of optically active α-fluorinated quaternary carbonyl compounds, with significant potential in drug discovery and complex molecule synthesis.

item.title: Black Titanium‐Oxo Cluster as a Dual‐Mode Catalyst for Regioselective Protein Editing
item.description:
A structurally engineered titanium-oxo cluster enables both photooxidative and hydrolytic modification of β-lactoglobulin—driving selective ROS-mediated oxidation under irradiation and protein hydrolysis at elevated temperatures.


ABSTRACT

Atomically precise titanium-oxo clusters are discrete molecular analogues of TiO2 and structural building blocks of many metal–organic frameworks. Combining features of homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, they provide a versatile platform for catalyst design. However, due to limited stability in aqueous media, they remain largely unexplored in biologically relevant catalysis. Here, we report a structurally engineered hexanuclear titanium-oxo cluster (tBu-Ti6) with promising photophysical properties, including a very low optical gap of 1.56 eV. Using β-lactoglobulin as a model protein, we demonstrate that tBu-Ti6 is an effective heterogeneous catalyst in aqueous solution, promoting both hydrolytic and photooxidative protein cleavage via two distinct pathways: Lewis acid-mediated hydrolysis and reactive oxygen species-driven photocatalysis. Nano-scale liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (nLC-MS/MS) reveals preferential cleavage near negatively charged regions of the protein, indicating electrostatic substrate recognition. Under 370 nm irradiation, tBu-Ti6 induces oxidation of tyrosine, tryptophan, and methionine residues in the intact β-lactoglobulin, underscoring its potential as a photocatalyst for selective protein modifications. During reactions in aqueous solutions, the cluster remains structurally intact, shows no decomposition or dissolution, and is reusable without loss of activity. Together, these results establish TOCs as versatile molecular catalysts for controlled protein modifications and underscore their potential in bioinspired catalysis.

item.title: Rational Design of a Chiral Hybrid Ge(II) Halide With Giant Chiroptical Activity for Circularly Polarized Light Detection
item.description:
Due to the stereochemical activity of the Ge2+ 4s2 lone-pair, the strong lone-pair expression in chiral hybrid (R/S-MBA)GeI3 halides induces remarkable chirality-favoring distortions, including a large asymmetric bond angle variance and projected deflection angle of the chiral [–Ge–I–]∞ chains. These structural distortions collectively enhance the intrinsic chiroptical activity, enabling high-performance circularly polarized light detection.


ABSTRACT

Chiral hybrid metal halides integrate semiconducting optoelectronic functionality with intrinsic chirality, offering new opportunities in the field of next-generation chiral photonics and spintronics. However, the incorporation of chiral organic ligands alone is often insufficient to induce pronounced chiral structural distortions, thereby limiting the resulting chiroptical activity. Herein, we demonstrate for the first time that the stereochemically active 4s2 lone-pair of Ge2+ can serve as an internal structural amplifier of chirality. We rationally designed and synthesized a pair of enantiomeric chiral hybrid Ge(II) halides, denoted as (R/S-MBA)GeI3 (MBA is methylbenzylammonium). Specifically, the strong lone-pair expression in (R/S-MBA)GeI3 drives significant chirality-favorable distortions, manifested by a large asymmetric bond angle variance and projected deflection angle of the chiral [−Ge−I−]∞ chains. This enhanced structural chirality increases the circular dichroism (CD) anisotropy factor (g CD) of (R/S-MBA)GeI3 to 2.66 times that of the Pb(II) homologs. Benefiting from the superior chiroptical activity, (R/S-MBA)GeI3 further exhibits second-harmonic generation (SHG)-CD anisotropy factor (g SHG-CD) values of −1.17/1.09, while the corresponding devices achieve photocurrent anisotropy factors (g Iph) of −0.403/0.391. Finally, we demonstrated a proof-of-concept circularly polarized light-encrypted optical communication system. Our work provides a new insight into the rational design of high-performance chiral functional materials.

item.title: Rare‐Earth‐Modulated Fe–Tb Dual‐Metal Single‐Atom Site Catalyst Enables Enhanced Activity and Durability for Acidic Oxygen Reduction
item.description:
Leveraging the oxophilicity of rare-earth elements, a rare-earth-modulated Fe─Tb dual-metal single-atom site catalyst was designed for proton exchange membrane fuel cells. The neighboring Tb single-atom acts as an “intermediate director” that promotes *OH desorption from Fe─N4 sites, alleviates high *OH coverage, and thereby enables stable and efficient acidic ORR.


ABSTRACT

The critical dependence on Pt in proton-exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) remains a bottleneck for commercialization. Single-atom-site catalysts, such as Fe-NC, show comparable activity for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in PEMFCs, yet their inferior stability constrains practical applications. In this work, we introduced the rare-earth element Tb as a single-atom site into the Fe-NC system and constructed a dual-metal single-atom site catalyst (denoted as FeTb-NC). Theoretical calculations and experiments suggest that Tb centers, with strong oxophilicity and unique electronic structure, synergistically regulate *OH binding on adjacent FeN4 sites, thereby lowering the energy barrier for *OH desorption. This elevates the activity of Fe centers and, more importantly, significantly lowers *OH coverage on FeN4, mitigating its detrimental effects. The optimized FeTb-NC catalyst displays improved performance: The half-wave potential is as high as 0.89 V (vs. RHE), retaining 88% of its initial current density after 100 h at 0.8 V. The PEMFC assembled with FeTb-NC as the cathode catalyst exhibits competitive performance and durability; the peak power density reaches 1.10 W cm−2 under H2/O2 conditions, and the device maintains 80% current-density retention after 100 h under H2/air conditions. This work offers new insights into performance optimization of Fe–NC-based materials and supports development of Pt-free PEMFCs.

item.title: Concentration‐Driven Solvation Reorganization Featuring Viologen Clustering Enables Air‐Tolerant Aqueous Organic Redox Flow Batteries
item.description:
Molecular-salt concentration induces viologen solvation transition, thereby improving redox stability in aqueous organic redox-flow batteries under ambient air.


ABSTRACT

Viologen derivatives are promising anolytes in aqueous organic redox-flow batteries (AORFBs), but long-term stability under ambient air remains challenging. Using 1,1′-bis[3-(trimethylammonio)propyl]-4,4′-bipyridinium tetrachloride (BVCl4), we show through physicochemical characterization and molecular dynamics simulations that increasing BV concentration beyond a critical threshold induces a solvation transition characterized by viologen clustering. Controlled O2 exposure of bulk-electrolyzed BV4+/BV3+• solutions using a carbon felt electrode, together with air-exposed AORFB full-cell cycling, shows that BV is converted to redox-inactive byproducts via OH–/reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated by BV3+•-O2 galvanic reactions and electrode-driven hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). The degradation is suppressed in a nonmonotonic manner governed by the solvation-transition threshold. We suggest that the enhanced air tolerance of concentrated BV electrolytes arises from this solvation reorganization, associated with viologen-clustering-induced steric shielding against O2/OH−/ROS attack and restricted BV hydration that limits Grotthuss-type OH− transport to reactive BV sites. Additionally, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance measurements at an Au electrode directly visualize BV2+ as the most degradation-prone state, forming redox-inactive deposits through reactions with OH−/ROS generated locally by HER and oxygen reduction reaction; this pathway is strongly attenuated once electrolyte solvation reorganizes. Voltammetry at an Au ultramicroelectrode further reveals that solvation-transition-driven clustering suppresses BV3+• disproportionation.

item.title: Surfactant‐Induced Morphology Reconstruction for High‐Performance Near‐Infrared Perovskite Light‐Emitting Diodes
item.description:
A homologous series of hydroxyl-functional quaternary ammonium surfactants reveals how alkyl-chain length governs perovskite crystallization, morphology, photon extraction, and charge transport. An intermediate chain length provides the optimal balance of these effects, enabling near-infrared PeLEDs with a peak EQE of 27.0% and strongly suppressed efficiency roll-off.


ABSTRACT

High-performance near-infrared (NIR) perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) require the simultaneous suppression of nonradiative recombination and efficient photon extraction, in which additive often play a vital role. However, molecular design rules that connect additive structure with both crystallization control and optical morphology remain poorly defined. Here, we employ a series of hydroxyl-functional quaternary ammonium surfactants—TMPAC, HDPAC, and DDPAC—with different alkyl-chain lengths while retaining a common polar headgroup. This molecular design reveals how hydrophobic-tail length regulates precursor organization and governs the balance among emissive quality, optical outcoupling, and charge transport. Increasing the alkyl-chain length alters the phase-conversion kinetics, suppresses lateral grain coalescence, and promotes anisotropic out-of-plane growth, thereby producing corrugated FAPbI3 films. The intermediate-chain HDPAC provides sufficient interfacial organization to improve radiative efficiency and photon extraction while maintaining favorable charge-transport balance. HDPAC-based devices achieve a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 27.0%, exhibit markedly suppressed efficiency roll-off, and deliver a maximum radiance exceeding 513 W sr− 1 m− 2. These results establish hydrophobic-tail length as an effective molecule-level modulator for coupling interfacial crystallization control with photon management in perovskite emitters.

item.title: Photoinduced Homolytic Carbon–Palladium Bond Cleavage of Zwitterionic π‐Allylpalladium Species and Annulation with 1,3‐Dienes and 1,3‐Enynes
item.description:
A distinctive annulation pathway for zwitterionic π-allylpalladium(II) species has been established through visible-light-triggered homolytic cleavage of the C–Pd bond, radical addition to alkenes, recombination with Pd(I), and Pd(II)-mediated conversion. The protocol possesses broad substrate compatibility, delivering various functionalized cyclic frameworks efficiently.


ABSTRACT

The zwitterionic π-allylpalladium species are versatile intermediates in modern annulation chemistry, yet their assembling partners have been largely limited to electrophilic reagents or dipolarophiles. Herein, we report a previously inaccessible (4 + 2) annulation reaction of common π-allylpalladium(II) dipoles with electron-neutral 1,3-dienes and 1-aryl-substituted 1,3-enynes via a distinct cooperative photo-induced pathway. Mechanistic studies indicate that the process proceeds through visible light-promoted homolytic cleavage of the allylic C–Pd bond to generate Pd(I) and allylic radicals, which undergo addition to polyunsaturated systems. Subsequent Pd(I)–radical recombination and intramolecular allylic substitution furnish a broad array of multifunctional oxa- and aza-heterocycles, as well as carbocyclic frameworks, in moderate to good yields. In addition, their assemblies with electron-poor dienes are also applicable, whereas the regioselectivity is distinct from that observed in traditional dipole-based annulations. Furthermore, the asymmetric version is successful by employing chiral bisphosphine ligands, with fair to good enantioselectivity achieved.

item.title: Programmable Amino Migration−Enabled Diversification of Allylamines
item.description:
A programmable radical migration strategy transforms allylamines into versatile synthons for divergent molecular construction. Controlled interception of a common translocated radical intermediate through complementary radical capture, atom−transfer radical addition (ATRA), and radical−polar crossover (RPC) pathways enables modular 1,2,3−trifunctionalization, providing rapid access to densely functionalized, C(sp3)−rich amino architectures.


ABSTRACT

Migration−enabled alkene functionalization offers an attractive strategy for accessing molecular architectures beyond the reach of conventional alkene transformations. Yet existing approaches typically channel translocated radical intermediates into a single reaction manifold, limiting the broader potential of migration chemistry for divergent synthesis. Here, we establish a programmable migration−enabled synthesis platform that redirects allylamines from passive alkene substrates into versatile synthons for divergent molecular construction. Through the integration of radical functionalization with amino migration, this strategy generates a migratory radical intermediate that undergoes selective diversification via complementary radical−trapping, atom−transfer radical addition (ATRA), and radical−polar crossover (RPC) pathways under mild photocatalytic conditions, enabling divergent 1,2,3−trifunctionalization of allylamines. Broad compatibility with radical precursors, bifunctional reagents, nucleophiles, and diverse allylamine scaffolds provides access to more than 70 densely functionalized, C(sp3)−rich amino architectures, including molecules bearing quaternary carbon centers. More broadly, this work establishes radical migration as a programmable design principle for molecular diversification and expands the synthetic utility of allylamines as modular synthons for the systematic exploration of structure−function relationships.

item.title: Gold‐Catalyzed “Anti‐Baldwin” Cyclization of Unactivated Alkenes
item.description:
A rare example of kinetically disfavored 5-endo-trig cyclization of unactivated alkenes is disclosed. The key to the success of this transformation is that the kinetically favored 4-exo-trig cyclization is reversible, thereby enabling equilibration to the thermodynamically favored 5-endo-trig cyclization intermediate, which then undergoes reductive elimination to form the product.


ABSTRACT

Owing to the unfavorable orbital alignments and geometric constraints, 5-endo-trig cyclizations are kinetically disfavored as stated by Sir Jack Baldwin. Consequently, reports of such cyclization are scarce and primarily rely on the use of activated alkenes. Herein, we report a rare example of “anti-Baldwin” cyclization of unactivated alkenes. The key to the success of this transformation is that the kinetically favored 4-exo-trig cyclization is reversible, thereby enabling equilibration to the thermodynamically favored 5-endo-trig cyclization intermediate, which then undergoes reductive elimination to form the product.

item.title: Short‐Range Molecular Ordering Enables Efficient and Stable Recombination Junction in Monolithic Perovskite/CIGS Tandem Solar Cells
item.description:
A short-range ordered molecular architecture is developed for the recombination junction in monolithic perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells. Locally ordered domains facilitate charge transport, while the surrounding disordered regions suppress ion migration. The resulting devices achieve a certified efficiency of 28.94% and retain 98% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point (MPP) tracking.


ABSTRACT

Monolithic perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells have made remarkable progress in recent years and are highly promising for next-generation photovoltaics. The recombination junction (RJ) linking the top and bottom subcells is an essential component that governs both device efficiency and operational stability. However, depositing a uniform RJ on the complex CIGS substrate while simultaneously achieving charge transport and operational robustness remains a formidable challenge. Here, we construct a short-range ordered (SRO) hole-selective architecture for the RJ by exploiting π–π interactions between a self-assembled molecule (SAM) and a polymeric SAM (PCCP). The SRO architecture shortens the intermolecular π–π stacking distance to accelerate carrier transport, while the surrounding amorphous regions effectively interrupt ion migration pathways. Furthermore, this strategy enables conformal coverage over the complex CIGS topography, improves interfacial robustness, and enhances structural resilience in service. Consequently, monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells employing the SRO-RJ achieve a maximum power conversion efficiency of 29.60% (certified 28.94%, 0.2036 cm2) and retain 98% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking. Our findings establish short-range molecular ordering as an effective strategy for engineering efficient and durable recombination junctions in monolithic tandem photovoltaics.

item.title: PCET beyond pKa: Disaggregation and Additional Base Effects as Neglected Key Factors for Unlocking Inaccessible Substrates in Direct Intermolecular Photocatalytic Ring‐Opening Remote Alkylation of Cycloalkanols
item.description:
Base effects beyond simple pK a relations enable redox-neutral ring opening of nonactivated cycloalkanols for remote Giese alkylations from previously inaccessible substrates. In-depth NMR studies have revealed the critical importance of the aggregation state and alcohol–base pre-organization to govern reactivity in such oxidative multisite proton-coupled electron transfer reactions (MS-PCET).


ABSTRACT

Photocatalytic oxidative multisite proton-coupled electron transfer (MS-PCET) reactions have emerged as a promising tool for the activation of strong O─H bonds in (cyclo)alkanols. However, these methods often require the use of e-rich arene-containing derivatives (para-methoxyphenyl (PMP), etc.) — a factor that greatly restricts their broader applicability. In this study, we report the successful implementation of targeted modulation of the base partner in photocatalytic cascade reactions of cyclic alcohols, unlocking previously rather inaccessible, nonactivated substrates. This approach successfully bypasses the prevalent limitations of ring-opening transformations of cycloalkanols by disaggregation of the bulk alcohol and strategic base selection. As a result, we here demonstrate an operationally simple and widely applicable protocol for the redox-neutral transformations of cycloalkanols into terminally C(sp3)-C(sp3)-coupled, functionalized open-chain products. NMR-based mechanistic studies, comprising in-depth H-bond analysis as well as DOSY and ROESY experiments, have elucidated the previously unrecognized crucial role of substrate disaggregation in this multisite PCET, along with (pyridine) base effects surpassing typical pK a-related and/or steric effects. Ultimately, our insights, for the first time, reveal the critical importance of the aggregation state and the design of productive alcohol-base pre-organization beyond pK a and enabled us to successfully pioneer remote alkylative Giese-type C─C-bond formations of previously challenging alkyl-substituted cycloalkanols.

item.title: Safranine T‐Derived Activable Photosensitizer to Synergistically Regulate the RSS/ROS Dynamic Equilibrium for Boosted Photosensitization
item.description:
A reactive sulfur species (RSS)-activatable photosensitizer triggers a three-step synergistic cascade: RSS consumption (Stage I), Photodynamic therapy (PDT) activation (Stage II), and massive reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst (Stage III). This three-stage synergistic cascade remodels intracellular RSS/ROS redox homeostasis, thereby dismantling tumor redox tolerance and greatly enhancing the therapeutic potency of PDT.


ABSTRACT

Photodynamic therapy (PDT) eliminates lesions like tumors via reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated oxidative damage. However, tumors overexpress reactive sulfur species (RSS) that scavenge cytotoxic ROS, endowing cancer cells with strong antioxidant resistance and weakening PDT efficacy. We fabricated a biosafe, readily available activatable photosensitizer ST-DNBS based on safranine T (ST). ST-DNBS selectively consumes RSS overexpressed in tumors and recovers photochemically active ST to produce massive ROS. For example, 6 µM ST‑DNBS depletes substantial glutathione (GSH), leading to a marked reduction in the characteristic absorbance of TNB2− (5-thio-2-nitrobenzoate dianion) at 412 nm in the DTNB (Ellman's reagent) assay relative to the control; ROS produced after 24 s of irradiation causes a 6.2-fold decrease in the UV absorbance of 1,3-diphenylisobenzofuran (DPBF). Tumor-activatable ST-DNBS depletes intracellular RSS to collapse tumor antioxidant systems, blocking ROS clearance and boosting intracellular ROS buildup. This RSS/ROS redox balance remodeling greatly enhances photodynamic activity, achieving a 90% tumor inhibition rate. Our RSS-scavenging, tumor-activated photosensitizer offers a practical strategy to overcome tumor antioxidant barriers and improve PDT antitumor performance.

item.title: Selective Reductive Amination of Long‐Chain Diols to Primary Diamines Over Nitrogen‐Modulated Ru0/Ruδ+ Dual Sites
item.description:
Selective reductive amination of long-chain bio-diols to primary diamines is enabled by N-modulated Ru0/Ruδ+ dual sites. Cooperative O─H and Cα─H activation accelerates rate-determining diol dehydrogenation, while interfacial Ru-Nx coordination weakens NH3 adsorption and suppresses carbon deposition, delivering 98.5% 1,9-nonanediamine yield with durable ten-cycle stability.


ABSTRACT

Linear primary diamines (DAs) are essential monomers for nylon and polyamide. Sustainable production of DAs from bio-diols via reductive amination (RA) requires to achieve the tandem diols dehydrogenation (rate-determining), aldimine condensation and imine hydrogenation, which remains challenging due to low efficiency, poor selectivity, and rapid catalyst deactivation under ammonia-rich conditions. In this study, we report an efficient and durable catalytic system for the RA of linear primary bio-diols to DAs by constructing a Ru n -N x -C catalyst with N-modulated Ru0/Ruδ+ dual sites. In the RA of 1,9-nonanediol, a high yield of 1,9-nonanediamine up to 98.5% is achieved under mild conditions (170°C, 0.3 MPa H2, 0.7 MPa NH3) for at least 10 cycles. Mechanistic studies reveal that Ruδ+ and Ru0 sites cooperatively drive diol dehydrogenation through O─H and Cα─H bond activation, respectively, while their synergistic interplay further promotes the subsequent RA toward DAs formation. DFT and AIMD simulations reveal that N-modulated Ruδ+ sites exhibit weaker NH3 adsorption than pristine Ruδ+ surfaces, thereby mitigating the excessive deposition of imine-derived intermediates and improving catalytic stability. Ru n -N x -C was further evaluated for the conversion of selected biomass- and polyester-derived substrates into value-added DAs.

item.title: Engineering Synthetic Molecular Operations Controlled by DNA‐Binding Proteins Through Templated Proximity
item.description:
DNA-binding proteins are harnessed as programmable interfaces that control synthetic molecular operations through templated proximity. Protein recognition induces spatial colocalization of split DNA components, triggering DNA strand displacement reactions that translate biological inputs into programmable nucleic acid processes. This strategy enables DBPs to perform modular bespoke operations, linking natural biomolecular recognition to synthetic information processing networks.


ABSTRACT

We describe a DNA-based molecular framework that enables DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) to perform diverse synthetic operations beyond their natural functions. We introduce templated proximity as a mechanism through which DBP–DNA recognition events are converted into programmable DNA strand displacement reactions. In this architecture, protein binding templates the spatial colocalization of split DNA components, generating functional nucleic acid outputs that can be propagated into downstream processes. Using representative DBPs, including EGR1, YY1, and p53, we couple protein recognition to DNA strand displacement, activation of a fluorogenic RNA aptamer, regulation of CRISPR–Cas12a and Cas13 activity, and DBP-triggered activation of hierarchical CRISPR cascades. These results establish templated proximity as a general transduction principle for integrating DNA-binding proteins into modular nucleic acid reaction networks and demonstrate that DBPs can function as programmable interfaces connecting natural biomolecular recognition with engineered DNA-based information processing, enabling modular communication layers with tailored synthetic functionality.

item.title: Selective Oxidation of Toluene to Benzaldehyde Driven by Electroreduction of Oxygen to Hydrogen Peroxide Coupled With In Situ Electro‐Fenton Reaction
item.description:
Cathodic electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide from oxygen reduction is coupled with in situ electro-Fenton reaction for selective oxidization of toluene to benzaldehyde, establishing a novel electrochemical process for the oxidation of inert C─H bonds.


ABSTRACT

Selective toluene oxidation is a pivotal reaction in the fine chemical industry. While electrooxidation at high anodic potentials shows promise, the low efficiency of the generation of reactive oxygen species limits the product yield. Herein, we describe a cathodic strategy for selective oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde via coupling the electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide from oxygen reduction with an in situ electro-Fenton reaction (eH2O2-EF). Among the different metal–nitrogen–carbon single-atom catalysts (M-NC SAC, M = Fe, Co, and Ni), Co-NC SAC stands out as the best catalyst, featuring a benzaldehyde selectivity of 90.63% and a yield of 21.9 mmol gcat−1$g_{cat}^{ - 1}$ h−1 at −0.3 V versus RHE with stable operation over 23 cycles. In situ spectroscopy and radical scavenging and quantification experiments indicate that the eH2O2-EF proceeds via toluene adsorption, ·OH-mediated oxidation, and desorption of products, where the ·OH generation and intermediate adsorption/desorption jointly determine the benzaldehyde yield. Theoretical analysis indicates that the Co-NC SAC thermodynamically facilitates H2O2 generation, accompanied by moderate benzaldehyde adsorption and an uphill further-oxidation step, leading to selective benzaldehyde production. This work establishes a novel cathodic paradigm for the selective oxidation of inert aromatic Csp3${{C}_{s{{p}^3}}}$-H bonds under mild conditions.

item.title: Covalent Organic Framework‐Templated Spatial Confinement of Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Perovskite Solar Cells
item.description:
We reported a covalent organic framework (COF)-templated spatial confinement (CTSC) strategy to regulate self-assembled monolayers in inverted perovskite solar cells; through suppressing molecular aggregation and improving buried interface uniformity, CTSC promotes compact perovskite growth, reduces interfacial recombination, and enables a best efficiency of 27.03% with enhanced long-term stability.


ABSTRACT

Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as efficient hole-contacting layers for p-i-n perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, incomplete SAM coverage and weak bonding with the substrate result in heterogeneous buried interfaces. Herein, a covalent organic framework (COF)-templated spatial confinement (CTSC) strategy is developed by employing a newly designed phosphonate–carbazole-based COF, namely COF-TPACz, to regulate the buried interface. The nanoscale island-like COF domains could restrict the penetration of aggregated SAM molecules and allow well-distributed ones to anchor on exposed substrates. Meanwhile, hydrogen-bonding and π–π interactions between COF-TPACz and SAM favor a more uniform molecular arrangement on the COF domains. These adjustments synergistically suppress molecular aggregation and improve surface coverage, yielding a denser and more homogeneous SAM interface.
